DATE:  April 8, 2025

TO:  Development Review Committee

FROM:  Valerie Chin, Assistant Planner

SUBJECT:  CASE NO. 32-25PPR – 1550 BONITA AVENUE– A REQUEST TO
  CONSTRUCT FOUR NEW BRONZE STATUES AT VETERAN’S
  MEMORIAL AT VETERAN’S HALL

SUMMARY
Yvonne Duran, representing the Community Services Department, is requesting approval
to construct four (4) new bronze statues at Veteran’s Memorial located at 1550 Bonita
Avenue. This building is located within the boundaries of the Official zone.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the Development Review Committee approve Case No. 32-
25PPR based on this staff report and the attached conditions of approval (Attachment 4
& 5).

DISCUSSION
On March 24, 2025, the applicant, Yvonne Duran, on behalf of the City’s Community
Services Department, submitted an application for the construction of four (4) new bronze
statues at Veteran’s Memorial at Veteran’s Hall. The statues are of a dog and three
soldiers, one of which is sitting in a wheelchair (Attachment 2). The statues are of varying
heights, with the two soldiers standing being the highest at approximately 5 feet 8 inches
tall. The exact locations can be seen in Attachment 1, and the layouts for the statue pads
can be seen in Attachment 3.

The statues will be located in the northeast corner, next to the existing Battle Cross statue.
The applicant is also proposing to add new concrete, as shown in the orange shapes in
Attachment 1. This new concrete will ensure that there is adequate space for pedestrian
movement, with the new statues being placed. The City’s Public Works Department will
be performing the work.

SURROUNDING USES
The project site is located within the Lordsburg Specific Plan area. The surrounding land
uses are mostly residential. Kuns Park is located to the northeast of Veteran’s Hall. The
proposed addition of the four (4) statues should not impact on the existing uses found in
the surrounding area, nor will they result in any impacts to parking, traffic, or circulation
at the existing facility.
 Case No. 15-25PPR – 1550 Bonita Avenue
April 8, 2025
Page 2

ENVIRONMENTAL ANALYSIS
This project is categorically exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act per
Section 15303 Class 3 in that the project involved the construction of a small structure
with negligible impact to the surrounding uses and environment. No further environmental
review is required at this time.

Dear applicant:

The Development Review Committee has considered your application for four (4) new
statues at 1550 Bonita Avenue. In accordance with Chapter 18.16 of the La Verne
Municipal Code, your project has been approved based upon the following findings:

1.  The subject application is consistent with the general plan and conforms
  to all specific plans, zoning, and other applicable ordinances and
  subdivision requirements and resolutions.

  The application is consistent with the City of La Verne General Plan, Municipal
  Code, and all development standards of the Lordsburg Specific Plan. The
  proposed additions will comply with all applicable standards.

2.  The site is safe, functional, and environmentally sensitive to the
  surroundings. Grading, where required, minimizes environmental
  damage to the extent possible.

  The site will remain safe and functional. The proposed statues do not have a
  substantive effect on site safety and function of the site.

3.  The architecture proposed observes community standards and protects
  the character of the adjacent development.

  The statues will be in character with the neighboring properties.

4.  The landscaping plan ensures visual relief, providing an attractive
  environment for the public’s enjoyment.

  No landscape changes are being proposed at this time.
 32-25PPR
April 8, 2025
Page 2

Approval of Case No. 32-25PPR is subject to the following conditions:

  1.  The applicant shall abide by the attached Standard List of Conditions.

  2.  Any revisions to the approved plans shall require review and approval by
  the Community Development Department.

  3.  The colors and materials to be used shall be in accordance with the
  approved colors and materials submitted by the applicant and on file with
  the Community Development Department. Any changes to the colors or
  materials must be approved by the Community Development Department.

  4.  The applicant shall restrict all outside and noisy construction activity to
  occur only between the hours of 7:00 a.m. and 8:00 p.m. or dusk,
  whichever is earlier, Monday through Saturday. No construction-related
  disturbances shall occur outside those hours or on holidays.

  5.  All requirements of the Building and Safety Department and Planning
  Department shall be complied with prior to the final approval of the
  proposed construction.

  6.  The enclosed affidavit acknowledging the above conditions, and the
  Standard List of Conditions shall be signed by the applicant and returned to
  the Community Development Department prior to the issuance of building
  permits.

  7.  The applicant must obtain building permits from the building department
  before the start of construction. The building department is open from 7:30
  a.m. to 12:00 p.m., Monday through Thursday.

The approval of Case No. 15-25PPR is subject to a ten (10) day appeal period
commencing from the date of this letter. Should you desire any further information,
please contact Valerie Chin of my staff at (909) 596-8706.

Sincerely,

Eric Scherer, AICP
Community Development Director
